content: A prospective survey was conducted to evaluate the public's response to unintentional poisoning incidents. The findings revealed that significant financial savings, amounting to €9,568,339.34 annually, could be achieved by encouraging individuals to first contact poison centers for advice. In 2008, 546 inquiries about silica gel were received, with only 10% of reported cases requiring hospital visits. Timely advice from poison information centers effectively minimizes hospital referrals and healthcare costs, as demonstrated in a 2009 study from Norway. A satisfaction survey involving public callers and healthcare professionals (doctors and nurses) indicated that poison centers do not incur higher costs compared to the absence of such services. This survey, conducted in Sweden in 2002, included all poisoning cases, even low-risk ones, and highlighted the cost-effectiveness of poison centers. Another study in the United Kingdom in 2018 analyzed the impact of poison centers on healthcare costs. It found that consultations with poison centers or toxicological databases reduced hospital referrals by over 40%, preventing an estimated 41,000 emergency hospital visits annually. The cost savings from avoided emergency referrals exceeded the operational budgets of poison centers, demonstrating their cost-effectiveness. In Australia, a 2019 study analyzed the financial benefits of poison centers. It found that patients who avoided hospital admissions or emergency department visits saved SG$1,390, while those managed in emergency departments saved SG$1,170. Hospitals also saved SG$1,477 per case. These findings underscore the significant cost savings for both the healthcare system and individuals when poison centers are utilized. Two prospective surveys in Australia examined the public's behavior when contacting poison centers for unintentional poisoning. The first survey revealed that 19% of callers would have gone to the hospital if the poison center was unavailable. The second survey showed a 6% adherence rate to advice recommending home management. Without poison centers, healthcare costs would be three to four times higher. Poison centers provide a cost-effective means of managing incidents that require minimal treatment or reassurance, significantly reducing the financial burden on hospitals and emergency services.
